_comment: Capability evidence ledger (#441). One entry per advertised capability,
naming the tests that prove it at each layer and the revision they were
observed at. conformance/validate_capabilities.py checks these against
the tests CI actually collected — a test id that no longer exists, or a
layer with no test, fails the build rather than quietly meaning nothing.
Statuses: verified (evidence at every required layer, observed passing),
implemented-unverified (code exists, evidence does not yet), failing,
deferred (out of admitted scope for now; needs a waiver).
Layers mirror the instruments in docs/PARITY.md: model = I1 core unit
tests, format = I2-I4 round trips and oracles, bridge = I5 buffer
round trips on the GTK main thread, gui = I6 AT-SPI journeys.
This ledger starts with the capabilities whose evidence was produced at
the current revision. It is deliberately not backfilled from PARITY.md:
an entry here asserts that someone watched these tests pass on a named

Test ids are the ones the tooling prints: nextest's binary id plus the test path (letters-core::structured::tests::x for a crate's lib tests, letters-core::docx::x for its tests/docx.rs target, letters::bin/letters::bridge::tests::x for a binary's), and the repo-relative pytest node id for a journey.
revision, which is exactly the claim the old checkboxes could not make.

features.title: Protected compound edits reject atomically with native feedback
features.scope: Protected range paste, clear, sort and row/column edits preserve content and history; unprotect restores editing. Does not certify XLSX protection-permission persistence or workbook structure protection.

features.title: XLSX cell lock and sheet permission state persists across edit/save/reopen
features.scope: Per-cell locked/hidden flags, style-default inheritance and modeled permission bits round-trip through the real XLSX path including later sheets; unsupported credentials warn with consent and cancel preserves source. Does not certify chart persistence, credential-bearing round trips or workbook structure protection.

features.title: Uninspectable sources block overwrite but permit explicit recovery copies
features.scope: Missing/corrupt imported source: ordinary and close-guard saves blocked; fresh-path recovery requires consent and retains edits on reopen. Rechecks destination after consent; not atomic concurrent-writer exclusion or complete package preservation.

features.title: Missing-image presentation warning allows cancel or explicit continuation
features.scope: Removing an inserted image triggers native warning before audience window creation. Cancel retains document and keeps show closed; Continue Anyway opens show. Does not certify image decoding or monitor privacy.

features.title: Double-click text editing commits multiline text with undo and cancel
features.scope: Accessible plain-text editor; Ctrl+Return commits, Escape discards; undo/redo restores text. Edited title survives PPTX save and reopen. Does not claim rich-text selection formatting.

features.title: Insert Table places one table at the cursor
features.scope: One 3x3 table with empty cells, inserted on the line after the caret's paragraph (or in it when that paragraph is empty). No literal grid text is left as prose.

features.title: Tables survive the document/buffer round trip
features.scope: Table cells render as a pipe grid and capture back as (table, row, col) paragraphs with per-cell run styles, including CJK, emoji and RTL text. Prose containing pipes stays prose.

features.title: Table row and column commands act on the cursor's table
features.scope: Insert/delete row and column operate on the table containing the caret, and do nothing when the caret is outside a table.

features.title: List commands apply to the caret's paragraph
features.scope: Bullet/numbered toggle, indent, outdent and restart-numbering act on the paragraph containing the caret and render exactly one marker. Indenting body text does nothing.

features.title: Page breaks are paragraph state that survives a round trip
features.scope: Insert Page Break toggles page_break_before on the caret's paragraph, adds no document text, and survives capture through the page-break tag.

features.title: Sections give parts of a document their own page, columns and header
features.scope: Insert/Remove Section Break at the caret and Page Setup on the caret's section are one undo step each; each section lays out on its own pages; .docx (w:sectPr per section) and .odt (a master page per section) keep the sections through Writer both ways. Every break is a next-page break; continuous/odd/even breaks, unequal columns and numbering restarts are loss-reported (LET-005S).

features.title: Word count counts writing, not presentation
features.scope: List markers and rendered table grids are excluded; the label uses a plural form from gettext.

features.title: GUI journeys record what they assert
features.scope: Every journey can be recorded from the display its assertions ran against; failures keep their clip; the evidence bundle reports an unlabelled clip as unknown, never as a pass.

features.title: Jump to a named range from the name box
features.scope: Define Name captures the selection; typing the name in the name box returns to it, including after a jump far from the origin.
features.note: The stats journey and the far-jump guard both exercise the path that used to abort the app (#507): GTK's gtk_accessible_update_next_accessible_sibling() drops a reference to a parent accessible it does not own, so the grid was finalized while still parented.

features.title: A name-box jump announces the cell it lands on
features.scope: Jumping by cell reference or to a defined name updates the grid's accessible description to name the destination cell and its value, so a screen reader says where the selection moved.
features.note: The description previously named only the last committed cell, so a jump announced nothing. refresh_grid_a11y already existed and five call sites used it; jump_to_reference was the one that did not. Against the unfixed binary the journey fails with "last observed: 'cell B2: seven'" after a jump to D7, so the evidence detects the defect rather than passing beside it.

features.title: GUI setup fails loudly and cleans up after itself
features.scope: A display that never answers, a requested display number already in use, and a readiness probe that never succeeds each exit nonzero naming the cause; the EXIT trap still removes the run's temporary files and reaps the server setup started. Neither budget is marginal, and they are independent: starting a server and probing one that has already started are different costs, so a test that shortens one cannot starve the other.

features.title: Selection runs what a change could break, or everything
features.scope: A shared crate, the workspace manifest or lockfile, a harness path (the selector included), an unrecognised path and an empty diff all run every app's journeys; a diff naming only one app's paths runs only that app. The LibreOffice oracle's own pull-request filter is held to the same rule: it must cover every crate the oracle tests and every workspace crate those depend on, derived from the manifests rather than copied from the filter.

features.title: A journey that fails before its body still leaves evidence
features.scope: unittest skips tearDown when setUp raises, and the app is launched in setUp, so the whole class of startup failures used to retain nothing a reader could debug: in CI exactly one file (journey.mp4), and with video off not even a directory. The app's own stderr — where a startup panic names its file and line — was read only by the capture that never ran, so it reached neither the artifacts nor the run log. Capture is now a cleanup, idempotent with the tearDown path, and records per-artifact whether each one landed so a guarded capture cannot retain nothing quietly. It also keeps what the journey wrote, before the temp-directory cleanups that run next delete it, excluding XDG_CACHE_HOME by exact path so a mesa shader cache cannot bury the evidence; and a core dump where the kernel writes one, with core_pattern recorded either way because a pipe handler leaves no file a container can keep. A passing journey still retains nothing, a skipped one is not a failure, and an artifact that was never applicable is not reported as missing.

features.title: Every test that sits out a run says why
features.scope: The skip inventory comes from the test lister, not from JUnit: nextest omits #[ignore] tests from its report entirely, so a JUnit-based collector reports zero skips on a workspace with seven ignored tests. An ignored test with no reason, an empty reason, a reason no listed test matches, and a listing that covers nothing are each rejected; runtime skips contribute their JUnit message. A reason in one target cannot cover a same-named test in another.

features.title: LibreOffice reads what we write, and we read what it writes
features.scope: Text, styling and formulas survive a round trip through LibreOffice Writer, Calc and Impress in both directions, for docx/odt/xlsx/odp, plus the LibreOffice-authored parity corpus ratchet. Needs LibreOffice installed and REQUIRE_SOFFICE=1, so it runs in the nightly oracle lane and never on a pull request.

features.title: Saving replaces the file whole or not at all
features.scope: suite-common-core's atomic save, which every app's Save goes through: a failure at any point before the rename leaves the original file byte-for-byte intact and no temporary behind; a successful save replaces it in one rename; concurrent savers never expose a partial or blended file. In Letters, a failed save keeps the edits and the close guard. Not covered: recovery checkpoints (recovery.md, #1217) and remote locations.

features.title: In-place rich text: caret and range formatting as one text session
features.scope: DCK-007. Double-click opens a text session on the controller; keys select a word and Ctrl+B/U and the editor bar format only that range; Enter adds a paragraph; Escape cancels without trace, Ctrl+Return commits one undo step; document undo is refused while editing; the styled range is saved and reopened in PPTX and ODP and across formats. The complex-script/IME journey (tests/gui/test_decks_ime.py) is advisory: a real IME and Orca remain manual DCK-019 evidence.

features.title: Two Letters instances share, join and edit one paragraph live; bold applied by one shows on the other
features.scope: Letters built with the off-by-default collab feature, over the Durable Streams binding (Node reference server 0.3.9), driven through AT-SPI by two real instances. Does not certify Matrix (the two-heads banner and Resolve are letters.collab.two-heads-resolve), tables/footnotes/headers (refused), or a side-by-side recording (the run uses matchbox, which shows one full-screen window at a time).

features.title: A version that covers nothing the others hold shows the two-versions banner on both Letters instances; Keep Mine and Keep Theirs collapse it to one head with the expected text on both, Open Both opens the other version as its own document and leaves the shared session alone
features.scope: Letters built with the off-by-default collab feature, over the Durable Streams binding (Node reference server 0.3.9), driven through AT-SPI by two real instances plus a windowless third collabd (tests/gui/collab_peer.py) that joins without answering applied and saves a different .docx. The banner, the Resolve dialog's list, the page text of both instances and, for the version graph, the third sidecar's own heads event are read; Resolve is pressed on the sharer's instance only. Does not certify Resolve from the joiner's instance, a version with a table or other refused content (Keep Theirs refuses it), Matrix, or a side-by-side recording (the run uses matchbox, which shows one full-screen window at a time).

features.title: Dynamic-array functions spill as the inventory says and survive XLSX save and reopen
features.scope: The functions and shapes in docs/TABLES-DYNAMIC-ARRAYS.md, on the pinned IronCalc 0.9.1: values and shape of each spill, #SPILL! in every direction and its clearing, #CALC! for an empty result, recalculation with source edits and resizes, a source on another sheet, and one undo step per spill. XLSX writes each as an array formula marked dynamic (with the _xlfn. and _xlws. prefixes the newer functions need), stores only the anchor, and the spill is recomputed in full on reopening. Pinned limits: a spill past the grid is clipped with no #SPILL!, and the spill reference operator (E1#) yields the anchor alone. Two GUI journeys drive the visible grid: a spill through its blocking, clearing, undo and redo, and a FILTER from #CALC! to a spill and back as its source is edited and undone. Does not certify Excel itself or a Calc that evaluates these functions (24.8 and later); what a Calc 24.2 rewrite does is pinned in tables-core/tests/soffice_oracle.rs and described in the inventory, not cited here.

features.title: Comments are anchored threads: add, reply, resolve and delete, one undo step each
features.scope: Threads are marks on the text (RunStyle::comments) with their bodies in Document::comments. DOCX keeps them in the comments part with w:commentRangeStart/End and commentsExtended for replies and resolved; ODT in office:annotation ranges (loext:parent-name, loext:resolved); LibreOffice reads both back. LibreOffice 24.2 writes no reply parent to .docx for a document it read from .odt, so such a reply opens as a comment of its own on the same text. Print and PDF show no comments, as LibreOffice's do not; Markdown, HTML and text save the text after a warning. Does not certify comments on a table, header or footnote body.

features.title: Tracked insertions and deletions are marks on the text, reviewed and accepted or rejected with undo
features.scope: A change is a mark (RunStyle::revision) holding its kind, author and date; deleted text stays, struck through, until accepted. While tracking, typing is an insertion and deleting marks text deleted. DOCX w:ins/w:del and ODT change regions, read back by LibreOffice. Paragraph breaks and formatting changes are not tracked (a tracked deletion across a break keeps the break). Markdown, HTML and text save the text after a warning.

features.title: A table of contents is inserted, updated and kept by Word and LibreOffice
features.scope: Headings of levels 1-3 (Word's default) with their page numbers, regenerated whole by Insert and Update (one undo step each); never inside a table. DOCX keeps it as the TOC field around the entries, ODT as text:table-of-content. Markdown, HTML and text save the entries as text after a warning. Does not certify levels 4-6, custom TOC styles or a table of figures.

features.title: Date, person and link chips are inserted from @ and survive DOCX and ODT
features.scope: The @ menu offers the relative dates and any chip already in the document that matches what is typed; a chosen chip is one inline object, the caret steps over it and Delete removes it whole. The GUI journey proves the date chip; person and link chips are proved by the model and format tests, not by a journey. A chip is saved as its label and, for a link or person, as its hyperlink. DOCX keeps a date as a Word date content control and a link or person as its hyperlink in a tagged control; ODT keeps a date as a fixed text:date and a link or person as a named text:a (a name-only person as a bookmark). LibreOffice reads both back. Only date, person and link chips exist.

features.title: Footnotes are inserted at the caret, laid out at the foot of their page, and survive DOCX and ODT
features.scope: A footnote is a reference mark on a run plus a plain-text body in Document::footnotes; one undo step takes out the note and its mark. The layout puts the body at the foot of the page that references it and continues one that is too long. DOCX and ODT keep the notes through Writer both ways. This does not imply endnotes or a rich note body (a note is plain text).

features.title: A paragraph's named style is picked from previews and kept as a reference through DOCX and ODT
features.scope: Normal, Title, Subtitle, Heading 1-6, Quote and Code are picked from the style picker, restyle the caret's paragraph in the model and feed the outline sidebar. A file's own style names and heading looks are read and written back. A paragraph keeps a named-style reference, not the file's style-definition graph: there is no style editor, and a style's definition is not written back as one (docs/readiness-2026-09/letters-fidelity.md, scope of the model).

features.title: A paragraph's own text direction (right-to-left paragraphs) is not a Letters feature yet
features.scope: Right-to-left text is kept: Hebrew, Arabic and mixed lines save and reopen exactly, in logical order, and cross LibreOffice in both formats (letters-core::soffice_oracle::right_to_left_text_survives_a_conversion_between_the_two_formats). Pango and GTK pick each paragraph's direction from its first strong character. There is no control that sets a paragraph's direction, no writer stores one (DOCX w:bidi, ODT style:writing-mode), and a file's own direction is not kept. Promoting it needs a model field, both writers and readers, a control, a GUI journey and an oracle test in each direction.

features.title: Password-protected and encrypted documents cannot be opened or written
features.scope: Letters cannot decrypt a document and has no password prompt or encrypted save. A password-protected .docx (an OLE compound file, which a pre-2007 binary file also is) and an ODT with encrypted parts are refused by naming the password, never opened as garbage or with a ZIP or UTF-8 error (letters-core tests/hostile_packages.rs: a_password_protected_docx_is_refused_by_naming_the_password, an_encrypted_odt_is_refused_by_naming_the_password). Sheet and slide protection in Tables and Decks is a different, editing-only feature and is not encryption.

features.title: A styled Unicode document survives edit, undo, redo, Save As and a restart, as DOCX and as ODT
features.scope: Each journey opens an authored fixture (tests/gui/fixtures/styled-unicode.docx and .odt: CJK, combining marks, emoji, RTL, run and paragraph styles, a footnote, lists, a table, an image, a comment, a tracked insertion, a table of contents, a header, a footer and an A4 page), edits one paragraph, undoes to the exact opened model and redoes to the exact edited one, saves with Save As through the chooser, restarts on the saved file and compares the whole reopened model with the edited one. It checks that only the edited paragraph changed and that the source file's bytes are untouched. Four spellings are compared as equal because the app does: a heading is kept with the next paragraph whether or not the flag is set, black is the default colour, a heading level naming no size draws at the body size, and page lengths agree to a tenth of a point. This does not cover visual page geometry, collaboration or macro compatibility, and the LibreOffice per-field matrix is the oracle claims'.

features.title: A pivot table is made from a selected table in the window, refreshed after source edits, and its results survive XLSX save and reopen
features.scope: Insert Pivot Table over a selected table with a header row: rows by one field, optionally columns by another, one value summarized by sum, count, average, min or max, placed at a chosen cell outside the selection (two columns to its right by default). The controller writes it as one undo step. A pivot keeps its definition in the sheet and is rewritten only by Refresh Pivot Tables, as in Calc and Excel; a refresh follows changed figures, new groups and vanished groups, clears the rows the new table no longer covers, and is one undo step. XLSX saves the results as values and the save warning says the pivot definition is not kept; reopening gives the values with no pivot. Does not certify an OOXML or ODS pivot definition round trip, more than one row, column or value field from the dialog, or Excel pivot compatibility.

features.title: A chart is built from a selected table with titles and a legend, edited in place, and survives XLSX save and reopen
features.scope: Insert Chart reads the selection: one column over the first column's labels, or a table of a category column and a series per value column named by the header row (columns with no number are skipped). The dialog sets the chart's kind, title, axis titles and legend position, previewed through the renderer the sheet uses. Edit Chart opens the chart under the selected cell with those fields filled in and replaces it as one undo step, keeping its series. XLSX create, edit, save and reopen keep every admitted field including on a later sheet, and a foreign chart field Tables cannot hold is reported as a scoped loss. Does not certify choosing series or placement by hand in the dialog, a Calc rewrite of a generated multi-series chart (the render lab compares how tables/chart-multi is drawn), or Excel itself.

waivers.reason: Paragraph direction needs a model field, DOCX and ODT writers and readers, a control and tests in each direction; it was listed unavailable rather than half-wired. RTL text itself is kept and proved.
waivers.scope: Letters paragraph direction (DOCX w:bidi, ODT style:writing-mode). Does not cover RTL text retention, which is verified under the oracle.

waivers.reason: Decrypting needs a password prompt, the OOXML and ODF key derivation and an encrypted save. Encryption and signatures are deferred by decision (epic #1190), as they do not block dependable everyday editing. The refusal names the password, so a user is not left with a ZIP or UTF-8 error.
waivers.scope: Opening, editing and saving password-protected Letters documents. Does not cover Tables or Decks files.
